resolvedFindings.priorProblem: A partial visibility update could commit for a preserved legacy unsupported base, then fail response parsing with HTTP 500.
resolvedFindings.resolution: PUT validates the complete strict two-field ARS/USD and boolean state before UPDATE. Partial, invalid and caller-owned identity fields are rejected before accessing users.
resolvedFindings.verification: Source inspection only; the added legacy-state test was read, not executed by this reviewer.

inspectedChecks.detail: Only the authorized base currency ARS/USD and Patrimonio visibility are persisted. The literal cases require saved base/visibility, owner isolation and unchanged balances/history. No widget catalog, new financial policy or additional preference was introduced.

withAuth derives the owner from verified Auth; users queries filter user.id; strict input rejects user_id/id and other properties. The existing users ownership RLS is preserved, and the migration adds only column SELECT/UPDATE for the new boolean.

Settings sends its rendered user.id in X-Preferences-Owner. After verified Auth, PUT rejects a present mismatching owner with 403 before body parsing or users access. A matching or absent optional header retains normal verified-owner behavior; the header never selects the target owner. The old-tab A/current-session B rejection and matching/absent test sources were inspected.

Auth rejection/unavailability uses existing 401/503 handling; DB errors propagate to generic 500 and Dashboard unavailable. Saved preferences are parsed strictly without fabricated successful defaults after a failed read.

Preference writes update only the two users columns. Dashboard removes its recordNetWorthSnapshot call and retains skipDailySnapshot for portfolio reading. History is read and re-expressed without an added financial write.

SettingsForm and Dashboard Hero/Sticky are keyed by user.id so a different owner remounts their client state. Hero initializes and synchronizes its currency from saved props; the global zarix.networth.view persistence was removed. Visibility suppresses both Patrimonio displays.

The migration keeps the existing owner policies/column grants, gives the new boolean a true default and rejects new invalid base writes. Its mirrored schema section, safe projection and User/generated types include the boolean; no new credential column is projected.

Read the focused PGlite handler/RLS, Settings handler, real Hero SSR and Dashboard failure test sources. Their declared doubles and execution limits remain explicit. No test result is independently attested here.

limitations: This is static review of the pinned working-tree sources, not executed evidence or promotion of any original system case.
No tests, native PostgreSQL, GoTrue, PostgREST, browser, network request or running application were invoked by this reviewer.
Final focused test reports and later runtime evidence are intentionally not pinned or certified.

An existing unsupported legacy base remains unchanged and strict Dashboard reads remain unavailable until its owner explicitly saves a supported full preference state through Settings; the change does not silently normalize historical configuration.
The shared schema and generated-type file hashes identify their current complete bytes; only their presentation-preference changes were in this review's product scope.
